entry.text:
Q1: src/hub.ts:65 `static DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000)`; applied hub.ts:94 (room.nudgeAfterMs), persistence.ts:77 fallback. Takes effect: (a) silence nudge armNudge hub.ts:1036-1058, re-armed by every post hub.ts:985 -> in a 9-seat room any message resets it, so it only fires on true stalls; identical nudge capped at 2 (1055). (b) openings deadline hub.ts:136 (2x at creation), 1081 (1x from first opening, chat does NOT reset), 1093-1107 (warn once if unarrived, then another period). (c) server.ts:325,442,464 report the deadline in minutes to seats. Verdict: keep 3 min — nudge scales fine with seat count (more seats = fewer silences); openings reveal at 3 min may leave a slow 9th seat out of the blind reveal but they can still chat, and longer holds cost 8 seats' wall time.
Q2: only 'bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts' — scripts/offline-runner.mjs:64 and :78 (list spans 26-182; sort|uniq -c shows no other count>1).
Q3: src/server.ts:21 `MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000; // stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)`; enforced 348 (zod max) and 359 (Math.min). Still justified: the 60s client timeout is a client-side constraint; server-side hold_until_actionable loop (362+) gives longer effective waits without breaching it.

proposal.text:
Q1: src/hub.ts:65 sets Hub.DEFAULT_NUDGE_MS = Number(process.env.CHATROOM_NUDGE_AFTER_MS ?? 180_000) (also the legacy fallback at src/hub/persistence.ts:77). Verdict: keep 3 min for a nine-seat session. (a) Silence nudge, armNudge src/hub.ts:1036-1058: re-armed on every post (src/hub.ts:985), and identical nudges stop after two (src/hub.ts:1055), so with nine talking seats it rarely fires and does not spam; a shorter value would add noise, a longer one would delay the "propose a conclusion" prompt in a stalled room. (b) Openings deadline, armOpeningsDeadline src/hub.ts:1093-1110: 2 periods at creation (src/hub.ts:136), 1 period from the first opening (src/hub.ts:1081), one extra period if someone never joined (src/hub.ts:1103-1104); chat does not reset it, and a late seat can still speak, so 3 min bounds how long eight seats wait on one without losing anyone's voice. The value is also surfaced in hints at src/server.ts:325, 442, 464. No change; a test can still shorten it via the env var.
Q2: exactly one name appears more than once in offlineScripts: bench-build-oracle-audit.test.ts, at scripts/offline-runner.mjs:64 and :78. No other duplicates.
Q3: MAX_WAIT_MS = 55_000 at src/server.ts:21, comment "stay under typical MCP client tool timeouts (Codex 60s)". Still justified: it keeps each tool call 5 s under Codex's 60 s client timeout; the clamp is enforced at src/server.ts:348 (schema max) and :359 (Math.min), and longer effective waits are already served by the server-side hold_until_actionable loop (src/server.ts:362ff) within the same budget, so raising the cap would only risk client timeouts.

challenge.objection: "longer effective waits are already served by the server-side hold_until_actionable loop (src/server.ts:362ff) within the same budget" contradicts itself. That loop is bounded by waitDeadline = now + waitBudgetMs ≤ MAX_WAIT_MS (server.ts:359-360), so it never gives waits longer than 55s. It only absorbs non-actionable chatter inside the budget. The justification should rest on the client timeout plus the event-driven wake (hub.wait returns as soon as a message arrives, so the cap adds no latency; see the comment at server.ts:20).
